ClubCategory.description:
Club family used to key benchmark rows (ADR-010 §3).

``ALL`` is the club-independent fallback — tempo and posture key on it.
ClubCategory.title: ClubCategory

Measurement.description:
A quantity measured off one swing, carrying no claim about whether it is good.

Deliberately **not** a `CheckpointScore`: no band, no `passed`, no `score`. The distinction is
the point. A metric earns a verdict only once a population distribution exists to judge it
against (ADR-010 §2 — no score beats a wrong one), and until then it is data. Making that a
*type* rather than a convention means a measurement is structurally incapable of being rendered
as a fault, however it travels.

Recording them before they can be judged is what breaks the chicken-and-egg that kept this
panel at three checkpoints: bands are derived from a population of measurements
(`scripts/golfdb/derive_pose_metrics.py` -> `derive_reference.py`), so a metric that cannot be
measured without a band can never acquire one. It is also why a session's swings stay worth
re-analyzing later — the measurement is on disk even though nothing yet knows what it means.

detail.description: How and where it was taken — 'address window -> impact window', and any sign convention. A bare number cannot be re-derived or re-normalized later; this is what makes it auditable when a band is eventually cut from it.
detail.title: Detail

Measurement.title: Measurement

PracticeGoal.description:
The golfer's intent for a swing (ADR-009 §Concepts).

Selected at session level, overridable per shot. Defaults describe the PoC case:
Fundamentals mode, no declared shape, club-agnostic.
PracticeGoal.title: PracticeGoal

PracticeMode.description:
What the golfer is practicing (ADR-009), and whether the shot is tracked (ADR-034 §3).

Every mode is analysed on its own, mechanics and shot alike. Only `drill` is not tracked: a drill shot never enters club or player stats, the mechanics baseline or a shape topic. Tracked-ness is derived from the mode and stored nowhere.
PracticeMode.title: PracticeMode

ShotData.description: Metrics for a single shot. Units in field descriptions (ADR-004).

attack_angle.description: degrees, + = up (hitting up on the ball)
attack_angle.title: Attack Angle

carry_offline.description: yards, + = right — the ball's lateral distance off the target line at carry
carry_offline.title: Carry Offline

impact_position_v.description: the vertical partner of impact_position, in the source's own words
impact_position_v.title: Impact Position V

ShotData.title: ShotData

ShotProvenance.description:
How a shot was obtained, for sources that *infer* rather than *receive* metrics.

A shot read off a photograph is a measurement of a measurement: OCR can drop a digit
and produce a number that is wrong but perfectly plausible. Carrying the confidence,
the physics-check warnings, and the raw on-screen text alongside the metrics is what
makes a bad parse auditable after the fact instead of silently poisoning a session's
scores (ADR-014). Sources that receive metrics directly (R10, mock) leave this `None`.

corrections.description: Field name -> text, for M38's review-and-edit of a parse. Empty until M38 writes one.
corrections.title: Corrections

device.description: Device profile that parsed this, e.g. 'hd_golf'.
device.title: Device

fields_present.description: The ShotData field names whose tiles the parse located, blank or not. None means not recorded, not 'nothing located'.
fields_present.title: Fields Present

image_path.description: Where the image was read from.
image_path.title: Image Path

image_sha256.description: Content hash of the source image.
image_sha256.title: Image Sha256

needs_review.description: True when confidence fell below threshold or a physics check failed.
needs_review.title: Needs Review

parser_version.description: Which screen parser produced this record — an entry in SCREEN_PARSER_VERSION's ledger. 0 means unstamped, which is every shot frozen Python's parser wrote.
parser_version.title: Parser Version

raw_fields.description: On-screen label -> raw recognized text, exactly as read.
raw_fields.title: Raw Fields

warnings.description: Human-readable reasons this parse is suspect.
warnings.title: Warnings

ShotProvenance.title: ShotProvenance

ShotSource.description: Where a ShotData record came from — for provenance and debugging.
ShotSource.title: ShotSource

TargetShape.description: Intended ball flight. With `shot_shaping` it chooses which shape topic grades the shot (ADR-034 §5.3); a shape never declared is not graded.
TargetShape.title: TargetShape

UnscoredCheckpoint.description: One quantity that was attempted and not produced, with the reason.

detail.description: What was seen, in the words of the code that refused: for a photo-side reason, the tile's on-screen label and the text under it. The reason is what a consumer branches on; this is the part a human reads.
detail.title: Detail

name.description: For a photo-side reason, the `ShotData` field the tile would have filled (`spin_rate`), the vocabulary `devices.json` and `fields_present` speak; for a flight refusal, the flight measurement's name (`flight_carry_yds`).
name.title: Name

UnscoredCheckpoint.title: UnscoredCheckpoint

UnscoredReason.description:
Every way a quantity can fail to be produced. Closed, and reported rather than guessed (ADR-010 §2).

Rust's whole enum, so a superset of the swing schemas' copy: `printed_blank` and `misread` are the photo-side reasons, about reading the screen, and are written into a `ShotResult` and never into a `SwingResult`, because frozen Python reads `analysis.json` with the closed set that lacks them (ADR-035 clause 4).
UnscoredReason.title: UnscoredReason

description:
One shot, measured and flown from what its screen printed. Written as `shot_analysis.json`. [M35]

Rust's alone: frozen Python has no twin of it. Never carried in a `SwingResult`, so the photo-side `unscored` reasons never reach `analysis.json`.

analysis_version.description: Which generation of the engine produced this (`ANALYSIS_VERSION`). Defaults to 0, not to the current version, for `SwingBundleResult.analysis_version`'s reason: a file lacking the key must read as older than every engine, so the corpus excludes it as outdated rather than pooling a number nobody can date.
analysis_version.title: Analysis Version

intent.description: The goal the shot was analysed under. A record of the analysis: the shot's intent of record is its manifest's, which can change after this was written. No number here depends on it, because every mode measures a shot alike.

measurements.description: The shot's rows, then the flight's, measured over the analysed view: the shot with every field outside what the device printed and analysis may use set to null (ADR-034 §2). A field the screen did not print, or printed only to be shown, produces nothing here.
measurements.title: Measurements

notes.description: Everything that degraded, in order of discovery: ADR-014's needs-review note, then what the shell appends, such as a handedness or loft gap.
notes.title: Notes

photo_sha256.description: Content hash of the photo this was computed from: the entry's staleness check, against the manifest's photo hash. Null reads as stale.
photo_sha256.title: Photo Sha256

shot.description: The shot as stored, `shown_only` fields included, because the phone displays them.

unscored.description: What could not be produced, named and never guessed (ADR-010 §2): the photo-side refusals in the device's declared tile order, then the flight's.
unscored.title: Unscored

title: ShotResult
